title: Fourier coefficient of a support component
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For a function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, let its Fourier coefficient at a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$ be its inner product with the corresponding product of basis functions, and let its component on $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be the sum of the terms whose indices differ from the constant index exactly on $S$. The Fourier coefficient of this component at $a$ equals the coefficient of $f$ at $a$ if those indices differ from the constant index exactly on $S$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
The basis is indexed by $\iota$ and spans the real-valued functions on $\Omega$
The basis vector at the distinguished index is constant $1$
$S$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
